Doosan Fuel Cell.why: maker of PAFC and SOFC power-generation fuel cells; it names AI data centers' need for stable power as the growth axis of its industry and has since filed US data-center fuel-cell supply contracts (KRW 501.4 billion on 09-02-2026, KRW 322.2 billion on 09-15-2026) via its US affiliate HyAxiom
Doosan Fuel Cell.evidence: Demand for stable power solutions is growing fast around the rapidly growing AI data-center market, making the fuel-cell industry's growth axis clearer within this demand trend (Doosan Fuel Cell half-year report, DART 08-13-2026)

players.product: PAFC (phosphoric acid) and SOFC power-generation fuel cells, incl. fuel-cell systems for US data centers, plus long-term service agreements

quarterly_data.signal: H1 2026 half-year report (DART, filed 08-13-2026, consolidated): H1 revenue KRW 189,106M with an operating loss of KRW 52,205M (company text: revenue KRW 1,891 hundred million, operating profit KRW -522 hundred million); fuel-cell main equipment KRW 143,093M (75.67%) and long-term service KRW 46,013M (24.33%). Q2 alone: revenue KRW 44,258,911,484, operating loss KRW 50,913,804,627, net loss KRW 55,598,415,364. FY2025 revenue was KRW 454,795M with an operating loss of KRW 105,673M.
quarterly_data.figure: H1 revenue KRW 189,106M, H1 OP KRW -52,205M; Q2 revenue KRW 44,258,911,484, Q2 OP KRW -50,913,804,627

quarterly_data.signal: Order backlog at 06-30-2026 (KRW 100 million, ex-VAT): main equipment 1,208 (start of year 1,519; new/other +1,120; recognised as sales 1,431) and long-term service 19,302 (start 18,807), total 20,510 (start 20,326). Supply contracts in progress include Samchully ES (KRW 55,400M, 26,000M and 26,000M; the 26,000M contract's end date later moved to 10-30-2026), UH Power KRW 138,600M, Doosan Enerbility KRW 154,600M, Lotte E&C (amount withheld), Korea Engineering Consultants KRW 30,400M (03-19-2026) and Ansan Green Power KRW 60,800M (04-29-2026), plus 20-year LTSAs with power producers such as Korea Western Power, KHNP and Korea Southern Power.

Capacity and utilisation, H1 2026 (Iksan and Gunsan plants): capacity 115.0MW, production 98.4MW, average utilisation 86% (FY2025: 205.0MW capacity, 162.4MW produced, 79%). Korea's cumulative power-generation fuel-cell installations were 1,477MW at end-June 2026, of which the company supplied 731MW (50% share). SOFC: with Ceres Power it developed cell-stack mass-production technology, invested about KRW 1,550 hundred million in a 50MW line by end-June 2025 and began mass production in H2 2025; it pursues system and cell-stack sales. H1 raw-material purchases (MBOP, EBOP, cell stacks) KRW 236,148M, mainly from Hi-Air Korea, Destin Power and J&L Tech; 2026 average MBOP cost per unit up 3.5%, EBOP down 7.2%, cell stacks up 9.0%.
quarterly_data.figure: Utilisation 86% (98.4MW of 115.0MW); domestic share 50% (731MW of 1,477MW); SOFC line 50MW

quarterly_data.signal: Data-center demand (the company's own view in the report): demand for stable power solutions is growing fast around the rapidly growing AI data-center market, and the company says the fuel-cell industry's growth axis is becoming clearer within this demand trend; it expects power-generation fuel cells to keep growing on distributed-energy demand and is pursuing overseas business opportunities. It names Bloom Energy and FuelCell Energy as the few competitors with commercial technology. Its PAFC reaches 90% combined electric and thermal efficiency with 10-year core-part life guarantees; its intermediate-temperature SOFC is offered in combination with PAFC.

Customers, H1 2026: Samchully ES KRW 69,933M (37.0% of revenue) and Lotte E&C KRW 32,947M (17.4%); main customers are public and private power producers. Related-party sales to parent Doosan Enerbility (fuel-cell product sales) KRW 16,438,500,000 and to US affiliate HyAxiom, Inc. (semi-finished product sales, raw-material purchases) KRW 7,890,458,162, with purchases from HyAxiom of KRW 2,303,600,508. Since 04-24-2025 the company holds an exclusive licence to HyAxiom's PAFC technology for Asia and Oceania.
quarterly_data.figure: Samchully ES KRW 69,933M (37.0%); Lotte E&C KRW 32,947M (17.4%); Doosan Enerbility KRW 16,438,500,000

H1 2026 investment KRW 5,234M; R&D expense KRW 4,144M (2.2% of revenue).
